Checking Model Answers*

A model can handle hard questions and still report simple company figures wrongly. Join our live session on March 2 to see how a shared metric layer helps teams test answers before anyone relies on them. We show real checks, common failure cases, and a short demo with time for your questions at the end. Can't join us? Sign up to get the replay.

Posts & Tutorials

  
  
🔗 Note: if you don’t see links in this email, it’s also available on the web: dataelixir.example.com/archive/issue-100.html
  

How to Study Statistics in 2027

As assistants handle more of the routine analysis, which skills still matter most? This post compares three learning paths and explains why sound judgment, careful testing and clear writing remain useful. It ends with a practical reading plan for people who have only a few hours each week.
Alex Example
  

Curved Models in Practice: Parker’s Bowling Scores

A straight line captures the rough pattern in bowling scores, but it misses what happens near the limits. This walkthrough builds a model from simple physical assumptions and compares the two fits, showing where the extra structure pays off and where it does not.
Sam Placeholder Reed
  

A Starter Guide to Ocean Sensor Data

Public ocean sensors produce long, messy records that are hard to compare across regions. This guide explains how to align them, handle gaps and turn them into compact features. It covers the main open datasets, shows a few small examples in code and lists the limits you should know before you trust the results.
Example Lab | Robin Doe & Jamie Roe
  

Tips and Tricks for Cleaner Joins in plain SQL

The slow part of a large join isn't always the join itself. This article measures several common patterns, explains why some of them copy far more data than needed, and offers small changes that help.
Casey Sample
  

Is the tipping point next Tuesday?

Decades ago, a simple growth model predicted that the town’s traffic would become infinite on a specific day. This essay revisits the forecast, explains why it fit the early data so well, and shows what it teaches about extending a curve far beyond the points you actually have.
Seeing the unseen | Morgan Test
  

Building Better Helpers

ExampleCo tested whether small, focused datasets could make software assistants more reliable at routine tasks. Read what changed, which results held up on new examples and how the team measured them.

Data Visualization

  
  

Two Variables, Twice the Fun

Making a map that shows two variables at once once required many slow, careful steps, but newer tools make it far easier. This tutorial walks through color choices, legend design and common mistakes, with examples that show when a two-variable map helps readers and when two small maps are clearer.
Taylor Mapmaker
  

Typical Chicago Library Requests

In a large set of city library requests, the most frequent entry is not the most interesting one. This short analysis finds the requests that set each district apart from the rest of the city.
Jordan Chart
  
  
  

Tools & Code

  
  

Announcing ExampleDB 3.0.0 LTS

ExampleDB began as a small, local query engine, but with this release it adds long-term support, faster writes and a stable storage format. The announcement lists the main changes and upgrade steps.
The ExampleDB team
  

toolkit - for building reliable report writing agents

When your reporting code already works well, it’s wasteful to have an assistant rebuild it on every request. This package lets you wrap tested functions as tools, describe when to use them and check their output, so answers rely on logic your team has already reviewed and understands.
Acme
